test_policy.notes: JWU is test optional. Submitting SAT/ACT (or SAT Essay/ACT Writing) is at the student's discretion and students who do not submit scores are not disadvantaged in the review.

requirements.notes: Common Application or the JWU application; no application fee for either. Official secondary school transcript (with certified word-for-word English translation if needed); international applicants upload documents to the applicant portal and provide English proficiency proof. For the I-20, after admission: reservation deposit, passport page, certified bank statement or sponsorship letter covering one academic year (not older than three months), and a signed financial declaration. The pages read do not mention essays, recommendations or interviews for undergraduates.

deadlines.label: Early Action I (non-binding), fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Application and transcripts must be received by the deadline. The 2026-27 catalog prints no year, so the fall 2027 cycle is assumed. The pages do not give a separate international date.

deadlines.label: Early Action II (non-binding)
deadlines.notes: Fall applications received after Jan. 4 are reviewed on a rolling basis.

deadlines.label: Regular admission (rolling) closing date, fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Catalog: 'Regular admission applications are accepted through July 15'; admissions may extend deadlines. Spring-semester applications are due Dec. 1. International applicants need time for the I-20 and visa, so applying much earlier is advisable; no international-specific deadline is published in the catalog.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Applicants whose native language is not English must show proof via academic transcripts or testing; scores must be no more than two years old. Alternatives accepted: SAT EBRW 500, ACT English 19 (or section scores of 19), GCSE/IGCSE English grade 4 or C, IB English grade 4+, CSEC grades I-III, WAEC grade 6+, completion of listed ESL programs (Kaplan, EF University Preparation, ELS level 112), or a transcript from a listed majority-English-speaking country. Total ESL exemption may require meeting both overall and subscore levels; JWU can still require ESL classes in a weak area. An on-campus ESL program is offered at the Providence campus only.

english.notes: Undergraduate minimum 75; recommended section scores 15 or higher. Designated Institution code 3465.
For exams taken on or after Jan. 21, 2026: undergraduate minimum 4 (graduate 4.5). The page does not name the scale; 4 is on the new 1-6 scale. TOEFL Essentials minimum 8 is also accepted.
Undergraduate overall 6.0; recommended section scores 5.5 or higher. One-skill retake reports accepted.
PTE Academic online or at-home option; recommended subscores 43 or higher.

cost.notes: Providence catalog 2026-27 (estimated, subject to change): annual tuition $45,408; student activity fee $250; New International Student Services Fee $1,386 per year (the $476 new student fee does not apply to international students). Room only ranges $7,000-$16,000 depending on residence hall and occupancy; the Gold meal plan ($7,360) is required for new residential students (other plans $600-$6,212). Student health insurance $2,670. Room and board total, books and other costs are not given as a single figure, so they are not shown. ESL program students pay $5,250 tuition per semester and are not eligible for JWU scholarships or grants

aid.notes: The International Presidential Scholarship is awarded to incoming international students who show academic excellence; amounts vary (no figures published), renewable up to four years of full-time day study, and eligibility is decided during the admission review. Need-based JWU grants noted in the catalog exclude international students; whether any need-based aid exists for international students is not stated. Students in the ESL program are not eligible for JWU scholarships or grants. Visit scholarships (up to $5,000 for fall 2026 if visiting by Dec. 31) are open to domestic and international first-years.

sat.note: The catalog pages read do not print a SAT code; look it up in the College Board code search.

act.note: The catalog pages read do not print an ACT code; look it up at act.org.
